verdict: OK to lend in Rajkot pumps, motors and valves — pursue component and OEM suppliers with clean receivables; avoid pure government-tender players until their dues cycle is visible.
title: Rajkot pumps, motors & valves: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**Rajkot is a submersible-pump cluster: foundries and machine shops feeding small and mid-sized assemblers who sell through dealers and, increasingly, to government water schemes.** [1][2] Cash comes from converting castings, stampings, copper winding and bought-out motors into a finished pump, then collecting from dealers or from a state department. **The value sits in the impeller-and-motor design and in the dealer shelf, not in the casting.** So when a proposal lands, check whether the borrower owns a product design or is only a job-worker for a larger brand; if it is only a job-worker, ask who its top three buyers are and what share they take.

## Where cash actually sits
**Working capital is the whole game: inventory of castings and wound motors, plus receivables that stretch hard when the buyer is a state scheme.** Rating reports on this industry flag working-capital intensity and only moderate pass-through of raw-material inflation in a competitive market [10]. **Capex is modest — a CNC line or a test bench — so a term loan for a new shed is usually the weakest use of our money.** So when a proposal lands, check the receivable days split between dealers and government buyers; if government is above half of receivables, ask for the last three years' collection pattern and the name of each department.

## What has changed now
**The demand signal is genuinely strong: IIP for electrical equipment (NIC 28) is up 10.3% YoY and 10.4% Apr-to-date, and exports are up 19.8% Apr-to-date in USD [D].** Gujarat GST collections are running 11.9% Apr-to-date against India's 6.1% [D], so the local trading base is expanding faster than the country. **But the peer results show the trap: Shakti Pumps grew revenue 37.9% YoY to ₹858.67 crore in Q1 FY27 while PAT fell 46.72% to ₹51.59 crore [5].** Oswal Pumps grew FY26 operating income 44.3% to ₹2,064 crore but saw Q4 margins moderate to 23.2% on competitive tender pricing and input costs [7]. **Growth without margin is the pattern in this cluster right now.** Note the Rajkot IPO filing is from August 2025 and is a local signal only [3].

## Who to pursue, and how to grow safely
**Pursue the component makers and the mid-size OEMs selling through dealers — they price on brand and collect on dealer terms.** Avoid, for now, borrowers whose order book is dominated by state water schemes: Shakti's Karnataka order was about 35% of its order book while that state's dues hit record highs in January 2026 [6]. **Structure as a cash-flow loan against receivables and inventory, not a bullet term loan.** Take stock-and-receivable statements every month, plus a dealer-wise ageing; covenant that government receivables stay below a stated share of the book and that drawing power is reset monthly on fresh statements. **Ask for the margin trend each quarter — if operating margin slips below 9.5% on a sustained basis, that is the rating agencies' own negative trigger for this industry [8].**

## Early-warning signs
**Watch receivable days against the borrower's own prior year, not the industry average.** If dealer receivables stretch while sales grow, the growth is being bought. **Watch inventory of finished pumps: a rising finished-goods pile means the dealer shelf is full.** If a borrower's order book is growing but margins are falling, treat it as tender-led and reprice. **And watch any sudden equity raise to fund working capital — peers have done exactly that to support capex and higher working capital [9].**
watch: Operating margin below 9.5% sustained -> treat as rating-negative and reprice or exit [8]
Government share of order book above half -> ask for department-wise dues status before enhancing limits [6]
Finished pumps rising while sales flat -> stop fresh inventory funding
GST turnover falling behind bank credits -> ask for explanation and freeze enhancement
watch_note: Trigger levels are policy suggestions (analytical framing), not data.
news_why: Strong IIP and export data offset by peer margin compression and state-dues risk.
